VIKI Agent: proactive coding, with decisions that adapt

About 2 minutes 45 seconds, narrated by a generated voice, with English captions. VIKI is pronounced Vicky (VIK-ee). It shows the real app working through a scripted example, so the Learning numbers on screen are sample data, not anyone's real results.

While Proactive VIKI is on and not paused and an app window is open, VIKI Agent's Decision notices supported opportunities, weighs relevance and timing, and chooses whether to stay quiet, suggest work or start a chat for eligible work. Within the grants you set in What VIKI may do and their daily limits, that work can move forward without another prompt. The film follows Notice → Decide → Work → Learn, from an overview of the product through the app at work to feedback and local adaptation. Your vault supplies durable context, and VIKI Agent shows what Claude Code is doing and any permission it asks for.

02Complete narration

0:00

VIKI Agent is a proactive coding agent with a decision engine that chooses when to help, what to suggest, and which work may start. It brings Claude Code and your Markdown project knowledge together, so a useful next step can reach you before you ask. With proactivity enabled and the app open, it considers your goals, context, timing, and granted authority. It can stay quiet, surface a suggestion, or start eligible work. Your vault provides durable goals, tasks, sources, and decisions. VIKI turns that context into opportunities to move your project forward.

0:45

That includes proposing work beyond your task list. After repeated API reviews, VIKI offers to turn that workflow into a reusable skill. The launcher explains why and links to the source chats. Make this a skill prepares an unsent message for your review. Other offers help you learn from captured sources, run a retrospective, or improve Decision questions. These proposals stay in your hands. Now follow a separate coding task from context to result. A due vault task asks for positive checkout quantities. Ask first reserves mission starts for you. Allowed lets eligible work begin within your activity limits.

1:29

On its next decision cycle, VIKI starts without another chat prompt. The agent reads the task and code, then requests an edit. Independent work still respects native permissions: Allow once approves the edit, and running the test command needs a separate approval. The agent responses are scripted; the app workflow, disposable edit, and local checks are real. You can follow what happened and review the evidence before deciding what comes next.

1:53

Your responses also shape future decisions. Opening a suggestion, acting on it, or choosing Not useful gives VIKI feedback. With enough labeled decisions, local learning adapts the scoring weights; attention estimates also adjust. Learning shows what changed, the starting and current values, and the evidence behind them. You can turn it off or reset it. This adapts VIKI's decisions, without retraining Claude. Broader improvements to skills, knowledge, and Decision questions begin as drafts for review. Sensitive instruction and system files are excluded from knowledge upkeep. The optional starter supplies deny rules; your configured Claude Code hooks can block covered operations. Discover useful work. Delegate with control. Learn from the outcome. VIKI Agent.

03How new work is suggested

This part of the film shows one kind of suggestion: turning a repeated coding workflow into a reusable skill. After three chats that began with similar messages, the launcher offers a skill. Its card names the source chats, and its Why now line gives the reason.

Make this a skill puts a fixed instruction in the message box without sending it. The instruction asks for a skill draft and says not to create or change a file. When a draft comes back, you can send it to Approvals with Propose this skill. The film stops before Send.

The other offers the film mentions help you learn from captured sources, run a retrospective or improve Decision's questions. They only prepare a draft for you to send, or wait in Approvals, and VIKI does not start a chat for them on its own, even when Start chats to do work is Allowed.

04How decisions learn from responses

VIKI adapts how Decision scores items from how you respond, on your computer. Opening an item or acting on it counts as positive feedback, and Not useful counts as negative. Not now sets an item aside and counts as neither. Recent feedback also gives future Decision requests a little context.

With Learning on, VIKI updates its estimates every five minutes. From the first decisions it tunes when and how loudly it speaks up. Once 20 decisions made by the Decision model carry your label, at least three positive and three negative, it also fits the scoring weights and topic offsets within fixed bounds. Later decisions use the learned values while Learning is on. Decision combines the model's answers with these local weights; learning calibrates VIKI's own choices and does not train Claude or the model behind Decision.

Not useful records one piece of feedback and removes the card; it sends no chat message, and one click does not refit Decision.

The Learning screen shows numbers computed from 20 sample decisions: 17 marked useful and linked to a goal, and three marked Not useful and not linked to one. For example, the Linked to a goal? weight moves from 0.600000 to 1.266243.

Learning → Show all numbers exposes starting values, current values and supporting observations. Each question shows how useful each question has been. You can turn Learning off, or select Reset what VIKI learned to start its numbers over; your decisions and labels stay. Broader improvements to question wording, skills and knowledge go through review, and the numeric fit does not rewrite instructions or install skills.

05How the vault fits

Markdown files hold your project notes, decisions, source material and guidance, and stay usable outside the app. Selected note excerpts can enter conversations. Decision draws on supported vault and activity signals; that does not mean every file is scanned or every note is sent to a model. The vault diagram in the film is an illustration, not a product screen.

Chats run through the unmodified Claude Code with its applicable instructions, skills, hooks and permissions. Decision's optional model is TypeSafe's Decision model, a separate service with its own saved key, a Send level for how much it sees (titles, excerpts or sections), Never send and a fallback to VIKI's own rules. The app and your notes are on your computer, but chat replies come from the model Claude Code uses (your Claude plan, an API key, a cloud provider or a model you connect), and the Decision model is a separate online service, so not everything runs offline.

06Protecting valuable work

Different controls cover different actions. Configure them for the project and review the results.

ControlWhat it covers
Grants and daily limitsWhether VIKI may start a chat for a task. Ask first, Allowed and Off are separate choices, and Proactive VIKI is off until you turn it on.
Drafts firstOffers to improve skills, notes and Decision's questions prepare an unsent message or go to Approvals. VIKI does not start a chat for them on its own, even when Start chats to do work is Allowed.
Files kept out of upkeepKnowledge upkeep leaves out sensitive instruction files, system files and raw sources. It is not a sandbox around every Claude Code tool.
Starter deny rulesThe optional Start with VIKI starter supplies Claude Code deny rules. It ships no hooks.
Hooks you configureHooks you set up in Claude Code can inspect or block the operations they cover, and VIKI Agent shows the hook notices it receives.
Claude Code's permission prompts and StopThe film's Edit and Bash requests each need their own Allow once. A chat VIKI starts does not skip them. Stop halts a running conversation.
Evidence and reviewA changed file and passing checks let you inspect an outcome. They do not prove that every requirement or valuable source is still correct.

None of these layers promises to prevent every destructive change, loss of intent, outdated fact or unsafe command, and the film describes the hooks layer without showing a hook at work. Knowledge reviews and offers of reusable guidance support maintenance; they do not repair or expire all old knowledge automatically.

07The autonomous coding example

This separate example starts from a dated task in 10-projects/checkout/tasks.md. The app finds the due task, checks the grant and routes the permission prompts. With Start chats to do work set to Allowed, VIKI starts a chat for the task at its next check, with no prompt or per-task click from you. The film shortens the scheduled wait and labels the cut.

VIKI starts such a chat only while Proactive VIKI is on and not paused, an app window is open, the grant allows it and the daily limit is not used up; Claude Code's permission prompts still apply. At most two chats that Decision starts run at once, and VIKI starts none of its own while one is open, so one stays free for yours. The default grant is Ask first.

The chat's first message is generic; the agent reads the task note before it looks at the code. After you approve the Edit with Allow once, the edit changes checkout.py. After you approve the Bash request, python -m unittest test_checkout -v runs in that project: the positive, zero and negative quantity cases give two failures before the edit and all pass after it.

The conversation shows the test output. Its Manual chip is Claude Code's permission mode; it does not show how the chat started.
